neighbours.label: The completion piece of 'placenta' (plac|enta) and of 'chitin'/'chitosan' (ch|itin, ch|itos)
fire: Hormones secreted by the placenta keep the uterine lining intact.
After delivery, the placenta is examined for signs of infection.
In many mammals the placenta is disc-shaped and attaches to one wall of the uterus.
Blood vessels inside the placenta bring nutrients to the growing embryo.
Beetle wings are stiffened by chitin arranged in layered sheets.
The cell walls of fungi contain chitin rather than cellulose.
Researchers extract chitosan from crab shells for use in wound dressings.
A film made of chitosan can keep sliced fruit fresh for several days.
quiet: Hormones produced by the corpus luteum keep the uterine lining intact.
After delivery, the amniotic sac is examined for signs of infection.
In many mammals the gestation period is shorter than nine months.
Blood vessels inside the endometrium bring nutrients to the growing embryo.
Beetle wings are stiffened by keratin-like proteins arranged in layered sheets.
The cell walls of plants contain cellulose rather than lignin.
Researchers extract gelatin from pig skin for use in capsules.
A film made of collagen can keep a wound moist for several days.
